product.name: Example Checkout
product.overview: A desktop app in which workshop staff select one available tool and one borrowing member, review the pairing, and record a checkout asynchronously. Duplicate submission is prevented. Success preserves the exact completed pairing until staff deliberately begin another checkout. Failure retains both selections and allows retry, correction, or cancellation of the uncommitted attempt.

application.summary: One activity area and one workspace support the complete checkout task and its recovery paths.

shell.description: The application opens directly into the checkout workspace.

navigation.description: Checkout preparation, recording, results, and recovery remain in the same workspace.

areas.name: Checkout
areas.purpose: Record the borrowing of one available tool by one member.

features.name: Tool checkout
features.purpose: Prepare, review, and record a tool and member pairing with clear completion and recoverable failure.

surfaces.name: Checkout workspace
surfaces.purpose: Prepare a single pairing, review it, record it, and inspect or recover from the result.
surfaces.entry: Open with neither field selected. Cancel checkout and Begin another checkout also return here with empty selections.
surfaces.exit: The task completes within this workspace. After success, the completed pairing remains until Begin another checkout is activated.
surfaces.focusIntent: Use ordinary keyboard-operable selectors and commands with visible focus. Follow tool, member, and applicable commands in task order. Selection changes retain focus. Progress and results are announced without repeatedly moving focus. After cancellation or beginning another checkout, focus returns to the tool selector.

Use an ordinary labeled single-select control with native keyboard operation and visible focus.
Selecting or replacing a tool retains the member selection.

Use an ordinary labeled single-select control with native keyboard operation and visible focus.
Selecting or replacing a member retains the tool selection.

components.name: Checkout status
components.purpose: Communicate the outcome of recording independently of command availability.

behaviors.statement: Use one semantic status region for progress and results.
During saving, show and announce Recording checkout.
On success, show and announce Checkout recorded; keep this result and the exact completed pairing visible until staff begin another checkout.
On failure, show and announce Recording failed, retain both selections, and explain retry, correction, and cancellation.
Keep failure feedback until staff retry, change a selection, or cancel.
When a failed attempt is corrected, clear the old failure feedback and return the workspace to editing.
Do not repeatedly move keyboard focus when the status changes.

components.name: Record checkout
components.purpose: Record the reviewed pairing and retry a failed attempt.
capabilities: Begin asynchronous recording of the displayed pairing.
Retry a failed attempt using the retained selections.

behaviors.statement: Show Record checkout before recording; make it unavailable until one available tool and one member are selected.
Activation captures the currently displayed pairing and immediately enters saving before another activation can submit.
While saving, show Recording checkout and suppress pointer, keyboard, repeated, and queued activation of this command.
Maintain a coherent visible focus location when the command becomes unavailable.
After failure, use the same command with the label Retry checkout.
Remove the recording command after success so the completed pairing cannot be submitted again from that state.
Use ordinary command keyboard activation and visible focus.

components.name: Cancel checkout
capabilities: Clear the current uncommitted pairing and its feedback.

behaviors.statement: Show only while editing an uncommitted attempt or after failure.
Clear both selections and feedback, then return focus to the tool selector.
Do not expose this command during saving or after success.
Use ordinary command keyboard activation and visible focus.

components.name: Begin another checkout
components.purpose: Deliberately move from a completed checkout to a new empty attempt.
capabilities: Start a fresh checkout after success.

behaviors.statement: Show only after successful recording.
Keep the completed pairing visible until this command is activated.
On activation, clear both selections and completion feedback, then focus the tool selector.
Use ordinary command keyboard activation and visible focus.

alternateInputs.description: Focus the same selector and use its ordinary keyboard selection behavior.

conditions: The workspace is empty, editing, or failed; saving and saved present the selected tool as read-only information.

cancellation.description: Once a selection creates an uncommitted attempt, Cancel checkout discards the whole attempt.

canonicalInteraction.description: Choose one borrowing member in the labeled single-select control. A new choice replaces the previous member and retains the tool. Selection is unavailable during saving and after success.

alternateInputs.description: Focus the same selector and use its ordinary keyboard selection behavior.

conditions: The workspace is empty, editing, or failed; saving and saved present the selected member as read-only information.

cancellation.description: Once a selection creates an uncommitted attempt, Cancel checkout discards the whole attempt.

patternBasis.rationale: Choosing one value from a labeled single-select control is a familiar interaction.

actions.name: Record checkout
actions.purpose: Record the reviewed pairing once, including retry after failure.
actions.outcome: The pairing is recorded successfully and remains visible, or a failure leaves both selections available for recovery.

canonicalInteraction.description: Activate Record checkout after reviewing both selected values. The command is unavailable with incomplete selections. Activation enters saving immediately and prevents additional submission. During saving the command remains visible as unavailable Recording checkout. Failure restores it as Retry checkout; success removes it.

alternateInputs.description: Focus the same command and activate it using ordinary keyboard command behavior. The same availability and duplicate-submission guard apply.

conditions: The workspace is empty, editing, saving, or failed.

cancellation.description: An in-progress recording cannot be canceled through this workflow. Once failure is reported, Cancel checkout can discard the uncommitted attempt.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit submit command with a guarded pending state, retained-input failure, and stable completion is a familiar form interaction.

actions.name: Cancel checkout
actions.outcome: Both selections and the attempt's feedback are cleared, leaving an empty workspace.

canonicalInteraction.description: Activate Cancel checkout while editing or after failure to discard the uncommitted pairing and return focus to the tool selector.

alternateInputs.description: Focus the same command and activate it using ordinary keyboard command behavior.

conditions: An uncommitted attempt is being edited or recording has failed.

cancellation.description: This command immediately discards an uncommitted attempt.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit cancel command that clears an uncommitted form is a familiar interaction.

actions.name: Begin another checkout
actions.purpose: Let staff deliberately move from a completed pairing to a new attempt.
actions.outcome: A new checkout begins with neither a tool nor a member selected.

canonicalInteraction.description: After success, activate Begin another checkout to clear the completed pairing and confirmation from the workspace and focus the empty tool selector.

alternateInputs.description: Focus the same command and activate it using ordinary keyboard command behavior.

conditions: The current checkout has been recorded successfully.

cancellation.description: This command begins a new empty attempt after the completed checkout.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit next-task command after a stable success state is a familiar interaction.

flows.name: Record a checkout
flows.goal: Record the intended tool and borrowing member once and verify the exact completed pairing.
flows.trigger: A staff member needs to check out an available tool to a borrowing member.
preconditions: At least one available tool and the intended borrowing member can be selected.
flows.outcome: One checkout has been recorded for the reviewed tool and member. Its completed pairing remains visible until staff explicitly begin another checkout.

steps.action: Select the available tool to be borrowed.
steps.response: The chosen tool is clearly identified in the workspace.
The chosen member is clearly identified alongside the chosen tool so the pairing can be reviewed.

steps.action: Review the displayed tool and member, then activate Record checkout.
steps.response: Recording begins with the reviewed pairing held unchanged. Further submissions are suppressed. On success, the workspace confirms the checkout and retains that exact completed pairing.

alternates.condition: Staff identify the borrowing member before selecting the tool.
alternates.outcome: Either selection can be made first without changing the task. Select the remaining item, review both values, and record the checkout.

alternates.condition: No available tool or selectable borrowing member can be found.
alternates.outcome: The affected selector explains that it has no selectable choices. An existing selection in the other field remains visible. Select an available choice when one exists, or cancel an uncommitted attempt.

alternates.condition: One or both selections are missing.
alternates.outcome: Record checkout is unavailable, and the unselected field remains visibly unset. Complete both selections before recording.

alternates.condition: Staff notice the wrong tool or member before recording or after a failed attempt.
alternates.outcome: They replace the affected selection using its existing selector. The other selection is retained. Review the corrected pairing and activate Record checkout.

alternates.condition: Recording has started and its outcome is pending.
alternates.outcome: The exact submitted pairing remains visible. Selectors and recording activation are unavailable, and progress is communicated. Wait for success or failure. The workspace does not offer cancellation of an in-progress recording.
A persistent failure message explains that recording failed. Both selections remain unchanged. Retry with the same recording control, correct either selection, or cancel the uncommitted attempt.

alternates.condition: Staff decide not to proceed with an uncommitted attempt.

steps.response: Both selections and the attempt's feedback are cleared, leaving an empty workspace.

alternates.outcome: Cancel checkout clears both selections and the attempt's feedback, returning to an empty workspace. Staff can begin selecting a new pairing.

alternates.condition: A checkout has succeeded and staff want to record another.

steps.response: A new checkout begins with neither a tool nor a member selected.

alternates.outcome: Begin another checkout explicitly clears the completed pairing from the current workspace and restores empty selectors. Select the next tool and borrowing member.

decisions.candidate: One tool selector and one member selector.
decisions.rationale: Each selector owns an independently changing required value. The same selectors also support correction.
decisions.result: Keep two ordinary single-selection controls with keyboard equivalents under their canonical actions.

decisions.rationale: Both invoke recording for the displayed pairing; failure changes the existing command's context and label.
decisions.result: Use one recording action with disabled, available, and saving behavior, and a Retry checkout label after failure.

decisions.rationale: Cancellation has an outcome only for an uncommitted attempt and is not offered while recording is pending.
decisions.result: Show Cancel checkout only while editing or after failure.

decisions.candidate: Persistent command to begin another checkout.
decisions.rationale: This command is needed after success to preserve the completed pairing until deliberate continuation.
decisions.result: Show Begin another checkout only after recording succeeds.

decisions.candidate: Separate review navigation, review dialog, and confirmation step.
decisions.rationale: Both selected identities can be reviewed together in the same workspace before the explicit recording command.
decisions.result: Review remains part of the canonical recording step without additional controls or surfaces.

decisions.candidate: Separate progress, success, and error message components or repeated result notifications.
decisions.rationale: These are successive outcomes of the same recording attempt, while command availability has its own behavior contract.
decisions.result: Use one status component and retain the recording action's independent saving state.
